reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure,including dimension zero. Let mu be any finite measure on E. Write X=L2(mu;R) and Y=L2(mu;E) for the actual quotient spaces. Let D:X partial-linear[R]->Y be a real linear partial operator on a submodule domain,and assume D is closable. Assume its graph is exactly the smooth compactly supported gradient graph:for every a in X and H in Y,
  (a,H) in graph(D) if and only if there exists phi:E->R such that
    phi is globally smooth,
    phi has compact support,
    the representative of a equals phi mu-almost everywhere,
    the representative of H equals grad phi mu-almost everywhere.
The gradient is the actual Riesz representative of the Frechet derivative. For every real-valued f:E->R that is globally C1 and has compact support,there exist proofs hp of MemLp(f,2,mu) and hq of MemLp(grad f,2,mu) such that
  (hp.toLp(f),hq.toLp(grad f)) in graph(closure(D)).
MemLp asserts suitable measurability and finite L2 norm of the actual functions;toLp is their actual quotient embedding,agreeing almost everywhere with its input. Closability means the topological closure of graph(D) is single-valued,and closure(D) is that closed partial operator. Thus the graph membership relates the L2 class of the actual C1 function to the L2 class of its actual gradient. No membership is built into the operator definition.
The theorem supplies both function/gradient L2 membership and closure-graph membership. It does not construct D,assume the finite measure is a probability or absolutely continuous measure,assume D has dense domain,upgrade f to smoothness,choose a different output gradient,or assert a pointwise identity of all possible representatives.
objects: Finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel E;finite measure mu;scalar and vector L2 quotient spaces;real linear partial operator D with its submodule domain,graph,closability and topological graph closure;actual smooth compactly supported gradient graph;actual C1 compactly supported f and its Riesz gradient;MemLp proof witnesses hp,hq and toLp embeddings.
domains: E finite-dimensional real-inner-product with Borel measurable structure and possible dimension zero. mu is Measure E with IsFiniteMeasure,not a probability requirement. f,phi:E->R;gradient maps E->E. X=Lp R 2 mu,Y=Lp E 2 mu. D:X partial-linear[R]->Y. Graphs lie in X x Y and closure(D) is the same graph-closure operator. Equality to functions in the graph premise is mu-a.e. representative equality.
quantifiers: For every stated E,finite mu and closable D satisfying the all-a,H graph equivalence,and every globally C1 compactly supported f,there exist hp:MemLp f 2 mu and hq:MemLp(grad f)2mu such that the pair of their actual toLp classes lies in closure(D).graph. The graph equivalence universally quantifies scalar/vector L2 classes and existentially selects one smooth compactly supported phi representing both classes. D is supplied,not existentially constructed.
assumptions: mu is finite;D is a real linear partial operator and is closable;its entire graph is exactly the smooth compactly supported actual-gradient graph via simultaneous mu-a.e. equalities;f is global C1 with compact support. E has the stated finite-dimensional inner-product/Borel structures. No probability normalization,absolute continuity,dense-domain premise or pre-supplied L2 proofs for f/gradient is assumed.
conclusion: There exist MemLp proofs for the actual f and actual grad f,with (class(f),class(grad f)) belonging to the graph of D.closure through their hp.toLp/hq.toLp embeddings. All three facts concern the same actual f and gradient.
scopes: The conclusion is membership in the closed operator graph on quotient classes,not original D graph membership or pointwise equality for all representatives. Finite mu can be arbitrary subject to the supplied closability/graph assumptions. No existence or density theorem for D is asserted here. Compact support is the compact closure of nonzero support;C1 f is not assumed smooth. No extra measure,tilt,law,kernel or weak-test identity is added. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: The Lp exponent is exactly 2;f regularity is C1 and the initial graph tests are smooth. There is no numerical constant,positive parameter,normalizer or covariance coefficient. The actual quotient embeddings depend on f,gradient f,mu and their MemLp witnesses;graph closure is determined by the supplied D.
